title: Design: sutra_search_ast — structural pattern matching
description:
Design structural pattern matching with preset anti-pattern detectors for Rust + Dart.

**Open questions:**
- Rule format: hardcoded Rust functions per pattern (clean, proliferates) vs. tree-sitter query files (declarative, verbose, language-coupled) vs. mini-DSL (jcodemunch's path — flexible, you're inventing a language).
- Cross-language node-type abstraction — jcodemunch's "universal node-type mapping" is a big project. Recommendation: **skip it**, ship per-language rule sets.
- Which presets are actually worth shipping? Generic ones (god function, deeply nested, magic numbers) translate; language-specific ones are where the value is — `unwrap()` outside tests, `?` in `main`, missing `#[must_use]`, swallowed errors, hardcoded secrets, TODO/FIXME.

**Recommendation already in docs/feature-ideas.md:** ship ~10 curated Rust + ~5 Dart presets as hardcoded functions first. Mini-DSL only if usage justifies it.

**Output:** design doc in docs/plans/ listing the v1 preset rules + chosen rule format.

Reference: docs/feature-ideas.md → "sutra_search_ast".

acceptance_criteria.text: v1 preset list frozen (~10 Rust, ~5 Dart) with example detection logic each
Decision on whether to ship a custom-query DSL in v1 (recommend: no)
